findings.text: Provides the exec stack transfer step that relocates staged argument pages onto the user stack, iterating downward from the top of the argument page array to the page holding the current offset, copying each relevant slice to successively lower user addresses, then rebasing the recorded executable offset and publishing the final stack address to the caller.

Reports a user copy fault if any page slice cannot be written to the destination stack, aborting further copying and leaving the caller stack pointer unchanged, otherwise signalling success after all required slices have been transferred.

Offers a small loader read helper that pulls a file range into a supplied address through the generic file read path and refreshes instruction cache visibility over that range whenever bytes were obtained, propagating the underlying read result.

Exposes the generic file read entry that validates readability and destination accessibility, confines the request to the allowed range and maximum size, then dispatches to either the direct read operation or the vectored read operation through a synchronous adapter.

Enforces that reads require readable mode and readable capability, reject inaccessible destinations and out of range requests, truncate oversized counts, return invalid argument status when neither read operation exists, and on success generate access notification plus per task byte accounting while always counting the call.

Implements synchronous vectored read by initialising a synchronous control block at the supplied file position, binding a user buffer iterator as destination, invoking the vectored operation, asserting that no asynchronous queuing occurred, and writing back the advanced position.

Completes process stack construction for FDPIC ELF by publishing the saved auxiliary vector to the stack, reserving pointer arrays for environment and arguments plus the argument count, and asserting that the computed stack pointer matches the expected final value.

Derives argument and environment pointer tables by walking user strings from the recorded argument base, validating each string as non empty and within the per string limit, terminating both tables with null, and recording the observed start and end boundaries plus the final stack base in the memory descriptor.

Fails stack construction with a fault status on any user write failure and with an invalid status on empty or overlong argument or environment strings, succeeding only when every auxiliary entry, pointer, count and boundary has been installed.

Describes the FDPIC load sequence that counts loadable program entries, allocates and versions a load map sized to that count, delegates actual mapping according to the requested arrangement, then resolves runtime addresses for entry, program headers and dynamic section before optionally compacting the map on paged systems.

Translates file virtual addresses to loaded addresses by locating the containing load segment for each of entry, program header table and dynamic section, adding the segment displacement and adjusting for header offset where relevant, leaving the corresponding runtime address unset when no containing segment exists.

Rejects images with no loadable entries and images whose dynamic section is empty, misaligned to the dynamic entry size, or not terminated by a null tag, reporting a library format error and identifying the offending file by name and inode in the log.

On paged systems compacts the load map by merging a segment into its predecessor when both share the same virtual to actual displacement and the predecessor end aligns exactly to the successor start page, extending the predecessor length to cover the gap, alignment skew and successor length while decrementing the segment count.

For constant displacement without paging, reserves a single anonymous readable writable executable region spanning from the lowest virtual base to the highest virtual top, loads each file backed portion by file read, captures the header address when the file offset is at the start, zeroes any trailing uninitialised tail, and initialises code versus data boundaries from the first executable and non executable segments.

Maps each loadable entry independently through file backed memory mapping, deriving protections from readable writable executable flags, choosing base address and fixed placement from independent, honoured virtual address, constant displacement with first seen base, or contiguous advancing base policies, then recording segment address and virtual bounds, clearing leading misalignment when writable, and provisioning uninitialised tail storage differently on paged versus non paged systems before recording code and data boundaries.

Propagates mapping failures, user clear faults, and anonymous tail placement mismatches as errors, with distinct handling that avoids touching beyond the last file backed page on paged systems by mapping the remainder anonymously and only clearing the partial page tail when writable.

Defines the FDPIC process status note payload as a common status header followed by general registers, executable and interpreter load map addresses for debugger relocation placed immediately after registers, and a floating point validity flag.

Defines an in memory note descriptor by name, numeric type, payload size and payload pointer, with total encoded size equal to the note header plus the name length including terminator rounded up plus the payload size rounded up to a four byte boundary.

Encodes a note by emitting its header with name and payload lengths plus type, followed by the name bytes and padding, then payload bytes and padding, succeeding only when every emission and alignment step succeeds, with a helper that binds symbolic note names and types from a short mnemonic.

Initialises FDPIC core headers so the file header carries ELF magic with current class, data, version and OS identity, core file type, target machine, zero entry, header sized program offset, FDPIC core flags and caller segment count with no section table, while each note program header is marked as note type with given offset and size, zero virtual address, no memory size and four byte alignment.

Snapshots signal state by recording the delivered signal in both info and current fields, low words of pending and blocked masks, parent, process, group and session identifiers in the caller namespace, and CPU times using group wide totals for leaders versus per task totals otherwise plus accumulated child user and system times.

Builds process info by clearing the record, copying the argument area truncated to the fixed argument field with separators normalised to spaces and terminated, capturing namespace identifiers, decoding the thread state word into numeric state, single letter name and zombie flag, and recording niceness, flags, user and group identities plus command name, failing when the argument copy faults.

Requires read side RCU protection while dereferencing the parent task pointer to obtain the parent identifier and while accessing task credentials to obtain user and group identities, releasing immediately after each use with no other locking shown.
Defines per thread dump state as a linked list node holding an FDPIC status record, a floating point register image, storage for up to two encoded notes and a count of valid notes.

Collects per thread core notes by allocating dump state, filling common status and load map addresses from memory context, capturing the first register set, always emitting a process status note, then searching remaining register sets for an active floating point set and on successful capture marking validity and emitting a second note while accumulating encoded sizes.

Encodes large program header counts by pointing the file header section offset at a trailing location, declaring a single section header of null type whose linkage, info and size fields carry the extended numbering linkage, segment count and section count.

Writes core memory contents by iterating the collected virtual area metadata array in order and dumping each described range with its recorded size, returning failure on the first unsuccessful range and success only when all ranges complete.
Declares the default FDPIC base platform as null and defines personality selection as Linux with preservation of caller bits outside the personality mask.

States core and note ABI facts that core files use core type with FDPIC core flags and note program headers use note type with four byte alignment, while load map versioning and program entry types distinguish load, dynamic and note entries.
